ledger.x: 1825: a congress in Upper Peru declares Bolivia independent.
28 October 1836: Santa Cruz decrees the Peru-Bolivian Confederation at Lima.
26 October 1839: Bolivia leaves the dissolved Confederation.
1841: after Ingavi the Bolivian army invades southern Peru.
7 June 1842: the Treaty of Puno ends the war and the occupation.
27 March 1867: the Treaty of Ayacucho with Brazil.
14 February 1879: Chile seizes Antofagasta.
1898: Bolivia gives up its title to the Puna de Atacama to Argentina.
1898: the seat of government moves from Sucre to La Paz.
14 July 1899: the Republic of Acre is proclaimed against Bolivian rule.
15 March 1900: the first Republic of Acre ends.
November 1900: a second rising against Bolivia.
December 1900: Bolivia defeats the second rising.
6 August 1902: Placido de Castro's campaign begins.
17 November 1903: the Acre fighting ends with the Treaty of Petropolis.
17 November 1903: Bolivia cedes Acre to Brazil.

17 November 1903: Bolivia receives a strip from Brazil in the same treaty: 'in exchange for over 3,000 km2 of Brazilian territory between the Abuna River and Madeira River', GBP 2 million and a pledged railway from Riberalta to Porto Velho.
October 1904: Bolivia cedes the Litoral to Chile.
October 1904: the Chilean occupation of the Litoral ends in annexation.
1909: the Madre de Dios basin goes to Peru.
15 June 1932: the Chaco fighting begins.
12 June 1935: the ceasefire ends the Chaco War.
1935: Paraguay holds the Chaco Boreal.

wars.name: Peru-Bolivian Confederation war
wars.outcome: The Restoration Army under Bulnes and Gamarra beat Santa Cruz at Yungay on 20 January 1839; the Confederation was dissolved in 1839 and Bolivia resumed its own course (Velasco, 26 October 1839).

wars.name: War of 1841 between Peru and Bolivia
wars.outcome: Gamarra's invasion of Bolivia was defeated at Ingavi on 18 November 1841 (Gamarra killed); the Bolivian army invaded southern Peru, vacated Tacna, Arica and Tarapaca in February 1842 and retreated to Moquegua and Puno; the Treaty of Puno of 7 June 1842 ended…

wars.name: War of the Pacific
wars.outcome: Chile won: it seized Antofagasta on 14 February 1879, Bolivia withdrew after Tacna (26 May 1880), the 1884 truce left Chile administering the coast and the 1904 treaty ceded the Antofagasta region.

wars.name: Acre War
wars.outcome: Brazil won: the Treaty of Petropolis (17 November 1903) gave it Acre for over 3,000 km2 between the Abuna and Madeira rivers, GBP 2 million and a railway.

wars.name: Chaco War
wars.outcome: Paraguayan victory: the ceasefire of 12 June 1935 and the Buenos Aires settlement of July 1938 gave Paraguay three-fourths of the Chaco Boreal; Bolivia kept the land bordering Puerto Busch and river rights.

certainty.note: No treaty fixes any frontier before 1866; the Chaco, the Amazon and the Pacific desert are claims, and the Chaco block (Presidente Hayes to 1877, Boqueron and Alto Paraguay to 1935) is a claim map.

The 24th parallel with Chile (treaty of 1866, kept by the treaty of 6 August 1874) and the 1867 line with Brazil are treaty-fixed edges, but the Litoral is under Chilean occupation from 1879 and the Chaco and Acre are disputed; the era is…
Treaty lines with Chile (1904) and Brazil (1903); the Chaco Boreal frontier with Paraguay stays soft until 1935.
The Chaco front moved year by year; the July 1938 settlement fixed the line.
Treaty and demarcated lines; the final Chaco demarcation was signed on 28 April 2009.
